hints: Look first at the big, broad dip on the left side of the spectrum and match its position using the data table.
Now check the middle region around 1670-1750 for a strong carbonyl dip, and notice what is missing there.
Compare that combination of present and absent absorptions with the functional groups in the four structures to leave only one fit.
walkthrough:
**Spot the strong O-H absorption**

Look at the left side of the spectrum. There is a very broad, deep dip centred around 3200-3600 $\text{cm}^{-1}$.

From the table, that matches:
$$\text{O-H in hydroxy (alcohol) = 3200-3600 \text{ cm}^{-1}}$$
So L definitely contains alcohol $\text{O-H}$ groups.

**Check carefully for C=O**

Now look around 1640-1750 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ where $\text{C=O}$ for amide, ketone, aldehyde, carboxylic acid and ester would appear.

The spectrum is fairly flat with high transmittance there, with no strong sharp dip. There is also no broad carboxyl $\text{O-H}$ stretching from 2500-3000 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ on top of the $\text{C-H}$ peaks.

So L has no $\text{C=O}$ bond at all.

**Match to the structures**

The small sharp dips near 2850-2950 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ are $\text{C-H}$ (alkane), and the strong dips near 1040-1300 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ are $\text{C-O}$ of an alcohol, both consistent with a polyol.

Only a molecule containing hydroxy groups but no carbonyl or carboxyl group fits. That is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{OH}$ contains a ketone $\text{C=O}$ plus two alcohols. A ketone would give a strong sharp absorption at 1670-1740 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, which is absent in the spectrum.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CHO}$ contains an aldehyde $\text{CHO}$. An aldehyde would also give a strong $\text{C=O}$ absorption at 1670-1740 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, which is not seen.
options.C: Correct. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$ is a triol with only $\text{O-H}$, $\text{C-O}$ and $\text{C-H}$ bonds. This matches the broad hydroxy $\text{O-H}$ at 3200-3600 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, $\text{C-H}$ at 2850-2950 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, $\text{C-O}$ at 1040-1300 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, and the absence of $\text{C=O}$.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ contains a carboxylic acid. This would show $\text{C=O}$ at 1670-1740 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ and a very broad carboxyl $\text{O-H}$ from 2500-3000 $\text{cm}^{-1}$. Neither feature matches the spectrum, which shows only alcoholic $\text{O-H}$ and no carbonyl.
